_meta.purpose: Canonical per-job tier/model/locality classification for the June-15 cost re-architecture (docs/cost-rearchitecture-june2026.md). The single source of truth consumed by: (1) the supervisor ephemeral-mode model router (Lever B), (2) the scheduled-task roster setup (which job folds into which Cowork task), (3) local-offload wiring, (4) the mkt-* eliminations. Grounded in the 30d ledger (job-costs.ndjson) + each job's reasoning nature.

dispositions.scheduled: Tier S — runs as / folds into a Cowork scheduled task on the subscription (free). target = roster task name.
dispositions.local: Tier 0 — runs on the on-device model (lib/local-llm.mjs, Gemma). Free. Classification/extraction/flagging only (a RAM-constrained host = small model).
dispositions.realtime-api: Tier 2 — genuinely latency-sensitive; runs on the budget-capped API key. Keep volume low.
dispositions.eliminate: Tier 3 — pause, drop to weekly, or replace with deterministic code. ROI-gated.
dispositions.script: Tier C — runs as cron/launchd CODE, never dispatched to a supervisor (no webhook, no agent turn). `model` is the tier of its optional single tool-less judgment call made from inside the script (claude -p / max-judge), or null when the script makes no model call. webhook-auth.sh never sees these jobs. Added 2026-10-04 (determinism pass) to replace the mixed `eliminate`/`local` labels the scripted jobs had picked up.

_meta.models: opus = deep synthesis only | sonnet = digests/drafting/moderate reasoning | haiku = cheap classify/poll | local = on-device Gemma
_meta.mcp_manifest: OPTIONAL per-job `mcp` array declaring which MCP servers the job actually uses (vocab: tools, health, supabase-edva, gsc, chrome-devtools). tools+health are the universal baseline. Omit = 'the routed tier's default .mcp.json is fine' (no assertion). PURPOSE: make each job's MCP surface explicit + checkable via `bin/mcp-manifest-check` — it fails closed if a declared need can't be met by any tier, and flags jobs whose needs exceed their model-default tier (e.g. Chrome jobs → must route to `ops`, which webhook-auth.sh already does via override) plus per-tier servers no declaring job needs (trim candidates). NOTE: this is a declaration + audit layer only. Spawn-time enforcement (spawn ONLY a job's subset) is NOT wired — the supervisor runs one long-lived session per tier and spawns MCP servers once per session, not per dispatch; true per-dispatch subsetting needs the ephemeral-subprocess architecture (deferred, see architecture.md). Seeded 2026-07-08 on the 5 Chrome jobs.
_meta.status: v1 2026-06-06; LIVE since 2026-06-17 — the `model` field is now consumed by webhook-auth.sh tier routing: any job whose model is set and != 'opus' (except the Chrome/CDP jobs pinned to ops in webhook-auth.sh) dispatches to the ops-light (Sonnet) supervisor at :9082 instead of ops (Opus) at :9092. The `disposition`/`target` fields (scheduled→Cowork, local→Gemma, eliminate) are still aspirational and NOT yet wired. Not routed through this file: mail to the agent's own address runs in a stateless one-shot (bin/email-inbound-run, agents.json ops.emailInboundMode) and only escalates into ops; per-message Gmail triage is sent to ops-light by the ops supervisor itself (triage-route.mjs, agents.json ops.gmailTriageTarget). Jobs with disposition script never dispatch at all.
_meta.local: This installation's own jobs (and field overrides of kernel jobs) live in agent/local/job-routing.json, same shape; every reader sees the two merged by lib/registry.cjs (`node lib/registry.cjs job-routing`).

morning-digest.rationale: Script since 2026-10-04: bin/morning-digest-run via launchd ai.claude.morning-digest; one pick call. No supervisor dispatch. Before: Morning briefing; calendar/weather/tasks/news. Sonnet adequate.

nightly-review.rationale: 7d self-assessment (Tue). Needs deep reasoning. Weekly slot. 2026-07-28: NO LONGER webhook-dispatched — runs as a dedicated ephemeral `claude -p --model $EDVA_MODEL_OPUS (claude-opus-5-5 since 2026-10-06, pinned in agent/config/models.env)` via launchd (ai.claude.improvement-review), because `model: opus` here is only a TIER label and the heavy supervisor has run claude-sonnet-5 since 2026-07-02, so this was silently a Sonnet job. Chains improvement-plan on a clean exit.

improvement-plan.rationale: Acts on every ACTION ITEM of the weekly review: safe changes land through self-improve-auto-apply, complex or high-blast-radius ones become Face-ID cards in the Improvements channel (rubric schema v4, 2026-09-29) — authors real code changes to Edva's own source, so it gets the deepest tier. Chained by trigger-nightly-review.sh; launchd ai.claude.improvement-plan (Tue 10:30) is a safety-net slot.

cost-efficiency-review.rationale: DAILY review of WHERE the Max budget went — cost split by token type, measured context floor per supervisor, working window, compact/rotate churn. Added 2026-08-06 after one overnight window burned a large slice of the weekly cap, most of it cache traffic rather than work, and nothing noticed: nightly-review's cost lens is weekly and job-shaped, so it could not see a structural context-floor problem (a job re-writing a 100k prefix every dispatch looks like a job doing work). Improvement process → Opus 5 per the standing rule; `runtime: ephemeral-opus` because `model: opus` here is only a TIER label and the heavy supervisor has run claude-sonnet-5 since 2026-07-02. Launched by launchd (ai.claude.cost-efficiency-review, 02:37 local slot from edva-cron-slots), NOT cron — cron cannot unlock the keychain for a claude -p. The trigger gates below 20 dispatches/24h, so a quiet day costs nothing.

system-issue-review.rationale: Nightly root-cause pass over the system channel that authors real code fixes. Capped at 3 clusters/night. 2026-07-28: NO LONGER webhook-dispatched — runs as a dedicated ephemeral `claude -p --model $EDVA_MODEL_OPUS (claude-opus-5-5 since 2026-10-06, pinned in agent/config/models.env)` via launchd (ai.claude.system-issue-review{,-critical}), same reason as nightly-review. Its trigger's gate is unchanged and still decides whether to run at all.

hum.rationale: The 20-min proactive check-in tick — the single biggest token consumer. Bash-gated upstream (sleep/activity/meeting), so most ticks never dispatch; the ones that do are relevance-judgment + light research + a voice ping. Moved Opus→Sonnet 2026-06-19 (~1.67x cheaper). WATCH: hum's whole value is NOT interrupting the user unless it matters — if Sonnet over-pings or misses signal, bump back to opus (one-line revert). The hum harvesters already fork claude -p --model sonnet --effort low, so Sonnet is proven on the sub-tasks.

hum-ideation.rationale: Creative ideation. 4x/day → 2 scheduled slots. Candidate harvest can go local.

hum-daily.rationale: Script since 2026-10-04: bin/hum-daily-run. No supervisor dispatch.

hum-review.rationale: Weekly hum feedback review (Sun). Weekly slot.

hum-explore.rationale: Script: bin/hum-explore-run (replaced hum-canary 2026-10-07). No supervisor dispatch.

skill-repair.rationale: Same-day repair of a broken read-only browser action / page parser (jobs/skill-repair.md). Queued by lib/skill-repair.mjs requestRepair() from its producers (skill-health and the installation's event-listing ingest), dispatched by trigger-skill-repair.sh. Pinned to ops by config/chrome-jobs.json (needs the chrome-devtools MCP to read the live page). Runs only when something broke; capped at 4/day.

email-inbound.rationale: Triage/label/route batched on watermark. P1 re-scan folds in. Urgency flag is separate (local, realtime).
